headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 16 studies yielded an effect size of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.74–1.02), indicating no statistically significant association between lycopene and prostate cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 87.00%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
